MINUTES
  REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  OCTOBER 24, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 7:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG
  CHAIR SCHMITZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Ciarolla, Griggs, Martin, Shinn, Silvano
  Robinson, Schachter, and Schmitz
  Committee Members Absent:  Harik and Nilsen
  City Staff Present:  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE REGULAR MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22,
  2022
  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE AUGUST 22, 2022,
  REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.
5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  Audience Member Candy Young shared that an issue occurred while her
  daughter was riding in the top ring at Peter Weber Equestrian Center when three
  dogs on the landfill road were off leash. She stated the dogs ran down the hill
  towards the fence and spooked the horse. She shared that there were two
  individuals with the three dogs and the one who appeared to be the owner
  refused to put the dogs on leash saying there were no leash laws. She shared
  photos of the individuals and the dogs.
  Audience Member Pam Schachter asked if there is a way to have the area
  monitored to address the issue and shared that while on a trail the previous week
  an electric bike entered the trail behind her and spooked her horse.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022
  1
   CHAIR SCHMITZ directed staff to look into options to address the issue and
  bring the item to a future meeting for discussion.
6.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  HORSE SAFETY OUTREACH (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief review of the outreach plan referencing the
  trails pamphlet included in the agenda packet. She noted that updates were made
  to the pamphlet and thanked MEMBER ROBINSON for her feedback. Supervisor
  Pinuelas shared that information would be posted online and that a special web
  banner would be posted on the City’s homepage leading to the pamphlet
  information, which would also be shared through social media messaging. She
  added that she would be working with Superintendent Goldsmith to review trail
  head signage and update as needed.
  MEMBER MARTIN asked that information be added regarding wheeled vehicles
  such as bikes, strollers, etc. not being allowed on the trails.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ suggested that once posted, Committee Members could repost
  the messages to help spread the messaging.
  MEMBER ROBINSON asked if the outreach could include video messaging.
  Supervisor Pinuelas shared the posts would include written messages. MEMBER
  ROBINSON suggested short one-minute videos be created that could be shared.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ directed staff to look into options for videos and bring it back to
  a future meeting.
B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY SHELTER AGREEMENT
  Management Analyst Slawson provided an overview of the written report.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked about right of entry to inspect, how the public would be
  allowed entry to the facility, and who would manage monitoring entry. Analyst
  Slawson shared that it would be set up and run by Animal Control with
  Superintendent Goldsmith assigned as the City designated contact.

  MEMBER SHINN asked if a horse owner would be allowed to go in to check on
  their horse. Analyst Slawson responded that after the shelter has been
  established and the emergency has subsided, owners would be allowed to go in
  to check on and care for their horse.

  MEMBER CIAROLLA asked how horse ownership is proven for those who may
  not have documentation. MEMBER GRIGGS shared that she has put her
  information on her horses’ hooves using a sharpie in emergency evacuations to
  identify her horses. CHAIR SCHMITZ noted that this is a great tip that should be
  shared. MEMBER SHINN asked about a situation when the horse owner is not
  present to do that. MEMBER SILVANO mentioned that others present can assist.
  MEMBER GRIGGS shared barn managers or others can also help. MEMBER

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022
  2
   SILVANO mentioned microchips are helpful in this situation and explained that
  the City previously held microchip clinics for this reason. Analyst Slawson shared
  that shelter staff are very experienced in this area and said she could get more
  information regarding identification.

  MEMBER GRIGGS moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO to:
  APPROVE THE EMERGENCY SHELTER AGREEMENT AND
  RECOMMEND IT TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITES COMMISSION FOR
  REVIEW AND APPROVAL.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

C.  EQUINE EMERGENCY WATER CACHE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Management Analyst Slawson provided an update regarding the emergency
  water caches. She stated that the water caches had been established and placed
  in strategic locations for access. She noted one was placed at City Hall near the
  storage container in the parking lot adding that it was originally placed in
  Chandler Park but was considered safer in the lot as it might be too new for the
  horses at Chandler. She shared that another one was placed at Dapplegray Park
  near Palos Verdes Drive East and Palos Verdes Drive North, and another was
  placed near Masongate Drive at Latigo Lane.

  Analyst Slawson noted Superintendent Goldsmith would be adding security
  measures to the caches and that signage would be established soon along with
  placement of emergency and safety informational flyers near the cache in a
  display case.

D.  CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an overview of the written report.

  CHAIR SCMITZ agreed the suggestion of having corn pits separated by age
  ranges for the children.

  CHAIR SCMITZ commented on the suggestion to develop new activities for older
  recommended the consideration of a lassoing activity for the older children.

E.  REQUEST FOR PERMANENT RESTROOMS AT THE PETER WEBER
  EQUESTRIAN CENTER

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  MEMBER GRIGGS asked if as a comparison the cost of high-quality portable
  restrooms, the type often used for horse shows, had been researched. Peter
  Weber Equestrian Center Concessionaire Gil Houle shared that Superintendent
  Goldsmith had researched that option and received quotes of approximately

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022
  3
   $50,000 a year for rental of two stalls and did not include ramps which would be
  needed to be ADA accessibility.

  MEMBER SCHACHTER asked who would be paying the additional expenses
  beyond the $81,000 listed on the quote. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that
  those could be covered with Park Facility fees.

  MEMBER SILVANO asked if the funds used for the restrooms could affect other
  projects CHAIR SCHMITZ responded its possible. MEMBER SILVANO asked if
  this would be the best use of the funds. Supervisor Pinuelas shared that the
  Maintenance Superintendent completed an assessment concluding that new
  restroom facilities at a different locations is a better solution to the existing
  restroom issues. MEMBER SILVANO asked for clarification that the existing
  restrooms were an issue that required repair and would be a temporary solution
  while this would be a more permanent solution both being an expense.
  Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed and shared that the issue was discussed at the
  previous meeting and led to staff researching a portable restroom option.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that during the renovation it was known that there would
  likely be issues based on movement of the ground and there could be an issue
  with the restrooms. MEMBER SILVANO asked if there was potential problem
  with land movement with the proposed new location. PWEC Concessionaire Gil
  Houle shared that land movement would not be an issue as they will be placed in
  a stable area.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked Staff to verify the amount charged for tax and correct as
  needed.

  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS to:
  APPROVE THE PROPOSAL OF A NEW RESTROOM STRUCTURE AT
  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER AND RECOMMEND IT TO THE
  PARK AND ACTIVITES COMMISSION FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

F.  MEETING FREQUENCY (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that as the Committee was now meeting every other
  month, there would be no meeting scheduled for November unless there was a
  need to call a special meeting. She noted that the next meeting would be held in
  December and asked the Committee to consider whether or not to hold the
  December meeting as it would fall on December 26 and instead meet next in
  January. She added that the Committee could then continue meeting bi-monthly
  from January on.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022
  4
   There was a consensus of the Committee to cancel the December meeting and
  hold the next meeting in January and meet bi-monthly from that point forward.

G.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  No comment about this item.

H.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK ARENA RENOVATION (VERBAL REPORT)

  Item was continued to the next meeting.

I.  APPROVED HORSE TRAINER PERMIT CATEGORY AND FEES UPDATE

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report and shared that
  business licensing would be handled by a new vendor, HdL Companies.
  MEMBER SILVANO asked if the vendor would be handling all business licenses.
  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that they would, and that staff is looking to inform
  horse trainers and host an informational meeting via Zoom to answer any potential
  questions and that Staff will be available to assist as needed.

7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER GRIGGS shared that a home being remodeled with some work being
  done on the backyard and that and a significant amount of trash is being put on
  the lower Ferncreek Trail. CHAIR SCHMITZ asked her to share the property
  address with Staff.

  MEMBER BRTIS shared that a property owner had routed their drainage out
  onto the Botanic Garden Trail. CHAIR SCHMITZ asked her to share the property
  address with Staff.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

8.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

  NONE.

9.  ADJOURNMENT

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022
  5
   CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting at 8:10 p.m. to
  the next meeting scheduled to be held on Monday, January 23, 2022, at 7:00
  p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
  Community Services Supervisor
